name: Esther Mills
life: “I still remember the envelope my former wife folded backward.” Sunday often includes a stop at the window at Night Shift Donuts, where Esther knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I recognized the handwriting as my old wife's. We still use the same little double underline.
appearance: Esther has black hair twisted into a small knot, a wide brow and a narrow jaw, and a favorite piece of clothing, a narrow-striped sweater. It usually goes with a train token tied to a zipper pull. When somebody else has the floor, Esther draws breath as if to speak and lets someone else go first.
personality: Esther can be wonderfully decisive about an emergency and maddeningly undecided about a gift. This is because a person can say precisely what hurts and rarely says exactly what they want.
agenda: To return the handwritten invitation to the ex.
family: Cynthia Bloom is Esther’s cousin raised in the same household. Esther brings a spare shopping bag. Cynthia chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The crash anniversary*, Cynthia says, “I am arranging a meal instead of a ceremony.”
connections: Ren Trent. The old invitation helps an orchestra librarian make a new, personal one.
